On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.

No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Client data return/deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit provision to Section 14: on expiry or termination TrueLink provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then deletes and certifies deletion. The Agreement currently requires us to arrange a new hosting environment within 60 days but gives us no right to our own data or migration help, which is unworkable for borrower and loan data. We can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law.

input.quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale: Section 5(a) does impose a minimum monthly commitment on us (a floor for Hosting Services and for Support Services payable irrespective of actual usage), so this is not the preferred position of usage-only/ordered-services-only fees. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and is therefore not redlined: (i) the commitment is confined to the current 12-month term, because Section 13 (p0078) runs for one year and renews only in successive one-year periods with a 30-day non-renewal right exercisable by either party; (ii) Section 14 (p0079) gives us a unilateral at-will termination right, with services and the corresponding minimum continuing only until the last day of the month following the month of our notice - an exit stronger than a mere volume reduction on 30 days' notice; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums anywhere in the agreement, so terminating simply stops the minimum prospectively, which operates as a true-up rather than a penalty. This is well clear of the walk-away case of a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right. Two drafting points noted but not flagged as deviations under this rule: the minimum dollar amounts remain blank ($____) and should be completed with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature; and Section 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of both our right to supporting documentation and our right to contest charges, which is a billing-transparency point better addressed under the audit/disputes rule. The "not less than ____ months" of programmer availability in Section 4 (p0043) is a commitment TrueLink makes to us and runs in our favour, so it is not flagged.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

content.text:
My analysis is complete. The findings:

**The commitment exists** — § 5(a) (p0045) imposes a monthly minimum on Client ("not less than $____ per month" for Hosting and for Support Services), payable regardless of actual usage. So this is a genuine minimum purchase commitment on us, not a Vendor-side commitment (the "not less than ____ months" of programmer availability in p0043 runs in our favour and is not flagged).

**But the exit exists too**, which is what the fallback requires:
- **Limited to the current 12-month term** — § 13 (p0078) runs one year, then auto-renews in successive one-year periods, with either party able to give 30 days' notice of non-renewal. The minimum never extends beyond the term we are currently in.
- **Unilateral exit on roughly a month's notice** — § 14 (p0079) lets Client elect to terminate at will, with services (and therefore the minimum) running only to the last day of the month following notice. That is a termination right stronger than a mere volume reduction.
- **No shortfall penalty** — there is no make-whole, no accelerated payment of unused minimums, and no take-or-pay recapture anywhere. Termination simply stops the monthly minimum going forward, which is functionally a true-up rather than a penalty.

This lands on the fallback position, so under the playbook's classification semantics it is not redlined.

input.quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
input.rationale:
Section 5(a) does impose a minimum monthly commitment on us (a floor for Hosting Services and for Support Services payable irrespective of actual usage), so this is not the preferred position of usage-only/ordered-services-only fees. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and is therefore not redlined: (i) the commitment is confined to the current 12-month term, because Section 13 runs for one year and renews only in successive one-year periods with a 30-day non-renewal right exercisable by either party; (ii) Section 14 gives us a unilateral at-will termination right, with services and the corresponding minimum continuing only until the last day of the month following the month of our notice — an exit that is stronger than a mere volume reduction on 30 days' notice; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums anywhere in the agreement, so terminating simply stops the minimum prospectively, which operates as a true-up rather than a penalty. This is well clear of the walk-away case of a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right. Two drafting points noted but not flagged as deviations under this rule: the minimum dollar amounts remain blank ($____) and should be completed with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature; and Section 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of both our right to supporting documentation and our right to contest charges, which is a billing-transparency point better addressed under the audit/disputes rule than here. The "not less than ____ months" of programmer availability in Section 4 is a commitment TrueLink makes to us and runs in our favour, so it is not flagged.</parationale>

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no post-termination transition or data-return provision. Section 14 (Termination) only fixes the date services stop; Section 13 places the burden on Client to arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, without any TrueLink obligation to assist with migration or to return Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data. Section 10 (Confidentiality) contains no return-or-destroy mechanic, and Section 2(f) (backups) addresses only TrueLink's own backup practices. Nothing in the document reaches even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days). Inserted the preferred language after Section 14 — six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification (with a carve-out for legally required retention). The insertion sits in a surviving section under Section 24.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and Client data return/deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit provision to Section 14: on expiry or termination TrueLink provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then deletes and certifies deletion. The Agreement currently requires us to arrange a new hosting environment within 60 days but gives us no right to our own data or migration help, which is unworkable for borrower and loan data. We can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.; counterparty is TrueLink, Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.summary: Insert transition assistance and Client data return/deletion obligations into Section 14 (Termination).
input.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit provision to Section 14: on expiry or termination TrueLink provides up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates, returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and then deletes and certifies deletion. The Agreement currently requires us to arrange a new hosting environment within 60 days but gives us no right to our own data or migration help, which is unworkable for borrower and loan data. We can accept 90 days of assistance as a fallback.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) at Client's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at TrueLink's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return to Client all Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in TrueLink's possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing, except to the extent retention is required by applicable law.

input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no post-termination transition or data-return provision. Section 14 (Termination) only fixes the date services stop; Section 13 places the burden on Client to arrange a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, without any TrueLink obligation to assist with migration or to return Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data. Section 10 (Confidentiality) contains no return-or-destroy mechanic, and Section 2(f) (backups) addresses only TrueLink's own backup practices. Nothing in the document reaches even the fallback (90 days of assistance plus export within 30 days). Inserted the preferred language after Section 14 — six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification (with a carve-out for legally required retention). The insertion sits in a surviving section under Section 24.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: compliant (at the fallback).** No redline proposed.

**Summary of the review**

| Fallback element | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Commitment limited to current 12-month term | § 13 (p0078) — 1-year term, one-year renewals, 30-day non-renewal right for either party |
| Reducible / exitable on ~30 days' notice | § 14 (p0079) — Client's at-will termination; minimum stops end of the month following notice |
| True-up, not a penalty | No shortfall, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums anywhere in the document |

The minimum in § 5(a) is a real take-or-pay-style floor on us, so this isn't the preferred position — but because it can't outlive the current 12-month term and we hold a unilateral exit that switches it off on roughly a month's notice with no recapture, it meets the fallback on every material term and the playbook says not to redline it.

Two things I flagged in the rationale rather than as deviations, both worth picking up in the commercial pass:

1. **The dollar figures are blank.** `$____ per month` for both Hosting and Support. The classification holds only because the exit works; the actual exposure is unknown until those blanks are filled. They should be set against realistic baseline usage before signature — this is the single highest-value negotiation point left on the clause.
2. **§ 6 (p0047) carves the minimum fees out of our documentation and dispute rights.** We can't demand backup for, or contest, precisely the amounts we're committed to pay. That belongs under the audit/disputes rule, so I left it there rather than double-flagging the same commercial term.

I also checked and deliberately did **not** flag the "not less than ____ months" programmer-availability undertaking in § 4 (p0043) — that is a commitment TrueLink makes to us and runs in our favour. Similarly, the storage and bandwidth allotments in § 3 are service specifications, not volume caps on our usage. One drafting oddity noted in passing: the internal numbering is offset from the section headings, so § 6's reference to "the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" actually points at Support Services rather than Compensation, and § 2(c) and § 13 cross-refer to "Section 12" for termination when the termination provision is § 14.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 5(a) does impose a minimum monthly commitment on us (a floor for Hosting Services and for Support Services payable irrespective of actual usage), so this is not the preferred position of usage-only/ordered-services-only fees. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and is therefore not redlined: (i) the commitment is confined to the current 12-month term, because Section 13 (p0078) runs for one year and renews only in successive one-year periods with a 30-day non-renewal right exercisable by either party; (ii) Section 14 (p0079) gives us a unilateral at-will termination right, with services and the corresponding minimum continuing only until the last day of the month following the month of our notice - an exit stronger than a mere volume reduction on 30 days' notice; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums anywhere in the agreement, so terminating simply stops the minimum prospectively, which operates as a true-up rather than a penalty. This is well clear of the walk-away case of a multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right. Two drafting points noted but not flagged as deviations under this rule: the minimum dollar amounts remain blank ($____) and should be completed with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature; and Section 6 (p0047) carves the minimum monthly fees out of both our right to supporting documentation and our right to contest charges, which is a billing-transparency point better addressed under the audit/disputes rule. The "not less than ____ months" of programmer availability in Section 4 (p0043) is a commitment TrueLink makes to us and runs in our favour, so it is not flagged.

**Finding: missing (medium severity) — redline proposed and validated.**

**What I checked:**
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** — mutual confidentiality obligations only; no return-or-destroy mechanic on termination.
- **§ 13 (Term)** — actually cuts *against* us: it makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, with no corresponding TrueLink duty to help or hand back data.
- **§ 14 (Termination)** — sets only the date services cease.
- **§ 2(f) (Backups)** — governs TrueLink's internal backup practice, not Client access or export.
- Searches for "termination", "return", and "data" surfaced no transition, exit, export, or deletion language anywhere in the document.

**Why it's a deviation, not a fallback:** the agreement doesn't reach even the fallback position (90 days' assistance + export within 30 days). This is a hosting agreement holding borrower and loan data — including Credit Data, which § 10(c) deems Client Proprietary Information — so on exit we would have migration deadlines but no contractual right to our own data in usable form.

**Redline (inserted after § 14, preferred position):** TrueLink to (a) provide up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates on request; (b) return all Client Content, Credit Data and other Client data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days; and (c) thereafter delete and certify deletion in writing, with a carve-out for legally required retention (sensible given the regulated credit data). Placement is deliberate: § 24 provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination, so the new paragraph survives without needing a separate survival hook.

The comment flags 90 days of assistance as an available fallback if TrueLink pushes back on the six-month tail.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-f419dd9f","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 12(b) gives us only a breach-of-contract indemnity from TrueLink: it covers \"any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations.\" There is no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, and no TrueLink non-infringement warranty that a breach-based indemnity could bite on (Section 2 addresses only TrueLink's own IP rights and Client's domain-name searches, and Section 12's disclaimer strips implied warranties). Because the vendor indemnity excludes IP infringement, the clause fails even the fallback position, which requires a vendor IP indemnity. The imbalance is aggravated by the very broad Client indemnity in 12(a) (Client breach, Client Content, Web Site, product/service injury). Redline adds IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorized access to Client Content, and gross negligence/willful misconduct to TrueLink's indemnity, plus standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; we left Client's indemnity in place as the smallest edit reaching the preferred position on vendor coverage.","proposal":"Expand TrueLink's indemnity to cover third-party IP infringement claims, breach of law, data/Client Content compromise and gross negligence or willful misconduct.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-f77f13ee","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, buried at the end of the indemnity section) is one-sided: it caps TrueLink alone at 12 months' hosting and support compensation, while Client's liability — including under the broad indemnity in Section 12a covering all claims, losses and liabilities arising from Client's breach, the Web Site, Client Content and third-party injury — is entirely uncapped. That is squarely within walk-away territory (\"Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped\") and fails the fallback, which requires a mutual 12-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. There is also no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages anywhere in the document, and the vendor cap is further narrowed to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 only. The redline makes the cap mutual and of general application at the greater of 12 months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, adds the Excluded Claims carve-out (confidentiality/data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and confirms Client's payment obligations are outside the limitation.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual and of general application, set it at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, and place indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement, and there is no change-of-control language anywhere (searches for \"change of control\", \"merger\" and \"successors\" return nothing). The clause is mutual and includes an affiliate carve-out, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so any merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of Client's assets requires TrueLink's approval, and (ii) approval is absolute rather than subject to a \"not unreasonably withheld\" standard, meaning TrueLink could block our corporate transaction outright — this approaches the walk-away case of a consent requirement on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client on written notice, applies a reasonableness standard to consent, bars assignment by TrueLink to a Client competitor, and confirms a change of control of Client is not an assignment and gives TrueLink no termination or re-pricing right, reaching the preferred position with minimal change to the existing sentence.","proposal":"Add Client affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, reasonableness standard on consent, no competitor assignment by TrueLink, and confirm change of control is not an assignment or termination trigger.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-2488a3cd","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Mortgage Logic.com. The § 2(a) licence is expressly \"non-exclusive\" and, better still, affirmatively confirms that Client is not obligated to use the Licence and may acquire, develop or licence competing software and services (subject only to TrueLink's IP and the § 10 confidentiality obligations). The Client covenants in § 8 contain no sole-source or \"shall not procure from any third party\" language, and the only exclusivity-flavoured grant runs the other way (Client grants TrueLink a non-exclusive licence in Credit Data, which does not restrict us). This meets the preferred position of no exclusivity on Customer. Noted but not flagged: § 3(i) requires Client to order a TrueLink credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface. That is a narrow, channel-tied service requirement rather than a requirements/exclusive-dealing covenant — we remain free under § 2(a) to underwrite outside the Interface using other providers — so it sits well inside the rule and is a sub-element for commercial awareness only.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-9b26be90","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The only ownership provision is one-directional: section 2(d) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface (which is acceptable), but nothing confirms that we retain ownership of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or our borrower/loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of or a licence to the work product produced under the Support Services (section 4 programmer deliverables). The only Client-side ownership language is incidental — section 13 says we \"shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content\" on discontinuation of Hosting Service — and section 10 merely treats Client's Intellectual Property and \"all results of the Hosting and Support Services\" as our Proprietary Information for confidentiality purposes, which is not an ownership or licence grant. With no ownership of, or perpetual licence to, the deliverables we pay for and no Customer Data ownership statement, the clause set fails even the fallback, so we have inserted a reciprocal Client ownership provision (assignment of Work Product, licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, no joint ownership) immediately after the existing Ownership clause. Noted but not separately redlined: section 8(d) grants TrueLink a broad licence to exploit \"Credit Data\" — that is a term-limited licence over narrowly defined raw third-party credit data (archived and not combined with Client Proprietary Information) subject to the Non-Competition Agreement, not an assignment of our data, so it sits within the negotiated bargain.","proposal":"Add Client ownership of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property, Client data and Support Services work product, with assignment from TrueLink and a licence back for embedded TrueLink IP; no joint ownership.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-809f7af6","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination charge on us. Termination (§14) is by written notice with services simply continuing to the end of the following month, with no minimum-term buyout or termination fee. Compensation (§5) is limited to ordinary monthly fees for Hosting and Support Services actually requested (subject to a monthly minimum, which is a pricing floor rather than a liquidated damages amount), and the anti-spam covenant (§7) carries no per-message penalty or stipulated damages. Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalt\", \"damages\" and \"shall pay\" return no Customer-payable stipulated amounts. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is proposed. We note only that the monthly minimums in §5(a)/§6 are blank and are excluded from the documentation/dispute rights — a commercial point for the pricing rule, not an LD issue.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-cc9e26c9","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The § 2(a) grant runs to \"Client\" alone: our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not licensed, and there is no mechanism (the Exhibit A site-amendment right in § 2(b)(ii) covers locations only, not additional licensed entities) to add them, so the clause fails even the fallback of affiliate coverage on written notice. § 15 also requires TrueLink's consent for any transfer other than to a financially responsible affiliate, so the licence is not transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction as the fallback requires. The licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion (§ 2(c) ties it to the term, and the § 13 cut-offs are breach-based), so this is a deviation rather than walk-away. Redline extends the grant to our affiliates and contractors and adds mutual successor-transfer rights.","proposal":"Extend licence grant to Client's affiliates and contractors and permit transfer to a successor in an M&A transaction","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-81a93eb2","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on us, meeting the preferred position. Section 2(a) goes further and expressly confirms we are not obligated to use the licence and remain free to acquire, develop or license competing software and services, subject only to TrueLink's IP rights and our Section 10 confidentiality obligations — both ordinary carve-outs, not business restrictions. The only Client covenants (Section 8) concern legal compliance, access controls, content warranties and anti-spam, and the sole restriction in Section 7 is on spamming; none limits the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The reference in Section 8(d) to a separate \"Non-Competition Agreement\" operates as a limitation on TrueLink's use of Credit Data, i.e. in our favour, so it is not flagged; we note only that that separate agreement is not before us and should be reviewed independently. The licence scope wording (\"in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables\") defines the permitted use of TrueLink's own Interface rather than restricting our activities, so it is not a field-of-use covenant of the kind this rule targets.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-9718b410","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The Agreement meets the preferred position on both material terms. (1) Customer convenience right: Section 14 (p0079) lets Client terminate at will on written notice, with services simply running to the last day of the month following the notice month — an effective 30–60 days' notice, well inside the preferred 30-day / fallback 60–90 day window. No early-termination fee, penalty or liquidated damages appears anywhere in the document. (2) No Vendor convenience exit: Section 13 (p0078) sets a one-year term with automatic one-year renewals; TrueLink has no right to walk mid-term for convenience (its only unilateral cut-off is the automatic termination of Sections 2 and 3 on a Client breach or a breach of Sections 8a–8c, which is cause-based, not convenience). The term is 12 months, so the \"no convenience right in a multi-year term\" walk-away does not arise, and Client in any event has one. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Licence Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (for Mortgage Logic.com — "Client") 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings and recommended positions

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, **six require negotiation** (two critical, three high, one medium) and **two clauses are missing entirely**. The remaining ten items are compliant, several of them because the Agreement is either silent in our favour or contains vendor-side commitments that run to our benefit.

The commercial risk is concentrated in the **ri[REDACTED] architecture of Section 12**. The Agreement caps TrueLink's liability at twelve months' hosting and support compensation while leaving our own liability — including under a very broad indemnity covering Client breach, the Web Site, Client Content and third-party injury — entirely uncapped, with no mutual exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere in the document. That asymmetry is squarely within walk-away territory under our playbook. Compounding this, TrueLink's indemnity is limited to breach of contract: there is **no third-party IP infringement indemnity and no non-infringement warranty** on which a breach-based indemnity could operate.

Three further structural gaps warrant attention. First, **ownership**: the Agreement confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface but says nothing about our ownership of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property, our borrower and loan data, or the Support Services work product we pay for. Second, **insurance**: the word does not appear in the document, notwithstanding that TrueLink hosts our web site, Client Content and customer credit data. Third, **exit**: there is no transition assistance or data return obligation — Section 13 places the migration burden on us (30 days for a new name server, 60 days for new hosting) with no corresponding duty on TrueLink to assist or to return our data.

On the positive side, the Agreement is genuinely clean on several fronts we would ordinarily have to fight for: **no exclusivity, no non-compete, no non-solicit, no MFN burdening us, no audit rights against us, and no liquidated damages or termination fees**. Section 2(a) affirmatively preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services. Section 14 gives us an at-will termination right, Section 13 renews in one-year increments on 30 days' notice, and Section 6 gives us a vendor-side most-favoured-rate commitment and a one-year price freeze. California law and California courts sit at our accepted fallback. We recommend we do not disturb any of these.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 4 | High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 2 Licence |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Licence |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Licence |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 Licence |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client |
| 11 | Medium | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 12 Indemnity |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 Compensation |
| 14 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |
| 15 | Medium | MFN — MFN obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 Compensation |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant (at fallback) | § 5 Compensation |
| 17 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 8 Covenants and Warranties of Client |
| 18 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 12 Indemnity |

### 2.1 Deviations and gaps — what we changed and why

**INDEMN (critical).** Section 12(b) gives us only a breach-of-contract indemnity, covering "any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations." There is no third-party IP infringement indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, and no TrueLink non-infringement warranty for a breach-based indemnity to bite on — Section 2 addresses only TrueLink's own IP rights and our domain-name searches, and Section 12's disclaimer strips implied warranties. Our playbook fallback requires a vendor IP indemnity, so this fails even the fallback. The imbalance is aggravated by the breadth of the Client indemnity in 12(a). *Redline:* expand TrueLink's indemnity to cover third-party IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Client Content, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, plus standard notice, control and cooperation procedure. We left our own indemnity in place as the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position on vendor coverage.

**LOL-CAP (critical).** The only liability limitation, buried at the end of Section 12, caps TrueLink alone at twelve months' hosting and support compensation and is further narrowed to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 only; our liability is uncapped. There is no mutual exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. Our fallback requires a mutual twelve-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. *Redline:* make the cap mutual and of general application at the greater of twelve months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, add an Excluded Claims carve-out (confidentiality and data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirm our payment obligations sit outside the limitation.

**ASSIGN (high).** Section 15 is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control language in the document. The clause is mutual and carves out affiliates, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so any merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all our assets requires TrueLink's approval; and approval is absolute rather than subject to a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, so TrueLink could block a corporate transaction outright. *Redline:* add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Client on written notice, apply a reasonableness standard to consent, bar assignment by TrueLink to a Client competitor, and confirm a change of control of Client is neither an assignment nor a termination or re-pricing trigger.

**IP (high).** Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface, which is acceptable, but nothing confirms that we retain ownership of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or our borrower and loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of or a licence to the Section 4 Support Services work product. Section 13's statement that we "shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content" on discontinuation of Hosting Service is incidental, and Section 10 treats our Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" as Proprietary Information for confidentiality purposes only — which is not an ownership or licence grant. *Redline:* insert a reciprocal Client ownership provision immediately after the existing Ownership clause (assignment of Work Product, licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, no joint ownership). Noted but not separately redlined: Section 8(d)'s licence to exploit "Credit Data" is a term-limited licence over narrowly defined raw third-party data, archived and not combined with Client Proprietary Information and subject to the Non-Competition Agreement — within the negotiated bargain rather than an assignment of our data.

**LICENSE (high).** The Section 2(a) grant runs to "Client" alone; our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not licensed, and the Exhibit A site-amendment right in Section 2(b)(ii) covers locations only, not additional licensed entities. That fails the fallback of affiliate coverage on written notice. Section 15 also requires consent for any transfer other than to a financially responsible affiliate, so the licence is not transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction as the fallback requires. The licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion — Section 2(c) ties it to the term and the Section 13 cut-offs are breach-based — so this is a deviation rather than a walk-away. *Redline:* extend the grant to our affiliates and contractors and add mutual successor-transfer rights.

**WARRANTY (medium).** TrueLink's only express warranty (Section 9) is a Y2K date-processing warranty. There is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no professional or workmanlike services warranty, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair, replace, refund or re-performance remedy. Section 11's "same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" is a self-referential standard of care, not a warranty with a remedy, and the disclaimer — while carving out express warranties — leaves nothing meaningful behind. This fails the fallback of 90 days software / 30 days services with remedies. *Redline:* insert an express performance and conformance warranty at the preferred position (12 months software, workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws) with a repair, replace or refund remedy; the fallback period is negotiable.

**INSURANCE (missing).** A full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the miscellaneous provisions contain no coverage requirement. TrueLink hosts our web site, Client Content and customer credit data. *Redline:* new Section 31 after Force Majeure at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O including tech E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request — with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) flagged in the comment. The survival clause references "Sections 1 and 5 through 30"; a conforming cross-reference update can be handled administratively.

**TRANSITION (missing).** Section 14 fixes only the date services stop. Section 13 puts the burden on us to arrange a new name server within 30 days and new hosting within 60 days, with no TrueLink obligation to assist with migration or to return Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data. Section 10 has no return-or-destroy mechanic and Section 2(f) addresses only TrueLink's own backup practices. Nothing reaches even the fallback of 90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days. *Redline:* insert into Section 14 six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification, carved out for legally required retention. The insertion sits in a surviving section under Section 24.

### 2.2 Compliant items — noted, not redlined

- **MINCOMMIT** sits at the fallback and is not redlined: Section 5(a)'s monthly minimum is confined to the current 12-month term, we hold an at-will termination right under Section 14, and there is no shortfall penalty, make-whole or acceleration of unused minimums. Two drafting points: the minimum dollar amounts remain blank (`$____`) and should be completed with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage before signature; and Section 6 carves the minimum monthly fees out of both our right to supporting documentation and our right to contest charges.
- **RENEWAL** meets the preferred position on renewal length (one year) and customer opt-out (30 days). Short of ideal drafting, and available as goodwill asks if renewal economics are negotiated: no vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and no CPI/3% cap on renewal pricing, since Section 6 freezes Hosting Services costs for year one only.
- **T4C** meets the preferred position on both material terms. Noted: no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (largely moot, as Section 5(a) bills monthly with invoices paid 15 days after receipt, i.e. in arrears), and end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 rather than 90 days — mutual, operating only at natural expiry, and shortening it would cut back our own flexibility. **Section 14 is expressed as "Subject to Section 4 hereof," and Section 4 is not in the reviewed text**; cross-references in Sections 5 and 6 indicate Section 4 concerns minimum monthly fees rather than any limit on our termination right, but this must be confirmed on receipt of the full Section 4.
- **EXCLUSIVITY / NONCOMPETE.** Section 2(a) is non-exclusive and affirmatively confirms we may acquire, develop or licence competing software and services. Noted for commercial awareness only: Section 3(i) requires us to order a TrueLink credit report on each borrower for which underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface — a narrow, channel-tied service requirement, not exclusive dealing. The separate **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in Section 8(d) limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data (i.e. runs in our favour) but is not before us and should be reviewed independently.
- **AUDIT.** Silence is better than our preferred position; we should not introduce an audit right against ourselves. Verification mechanics run our way (Section 6 documentation and contest rights; Section 3(e) real-time usage statistics and raw log files).
- **GOVLAW.** California law and exclusive venue in San Luis Obispo County sit at our fallback, with no arbitration provision. Venue in TrueLink's local county rather than New York County is noted, not redlined.
- **MFN / NOSOLICIT / LD.** No customer-side parity undertaking, no non-solicit or no-hire covenant, and no liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination charge.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following must be resolved before we can recommend signature:

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12).** Our playbook identifies "Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped" as a walk-away. A mutual cap with the Excluded Claims carve-out, and a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages, is non-negotiable.
2. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE).** The absence of any coverage requirement for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory under the rule. We require at minimum the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
3. **No IP infringement indemnity (INDEMN, § 12).** The vendor indemnity fails even the fallback. Given the absence of any non-infringement warranty, we carry undiluted infringement exposure on a licensed Interface.
4. **Approaching walk-away — assignment consent with no M&A carve-out (ASSIGN, § 15).** An absolute consent right over our merger, acquisition or asset sale approaches the walk-away case of a consent requirement on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations and two missing clauses (INDEMN, LOL-CAP, ASSIGN, IP, LICENSE, WARRANTY, INSURANCE, TRANSITION), holding the four walk-away items as conditions of signature and signalling the stated fallbacks on warranty duration and insurance limits.
2. **Request the missing Section 4** and confirm that the "Subject to Section 4" qualifier in Section 14 does not constrain our at-will termination right.
3. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in Section 8(d), which is not before us.
4. **Commercial team to complete the blank minimum monthly amounts** in Section 5(a) and Section 6 with figures reflecting realistic baseline usage, and consider whether to press Section 6 to extend documentation and contest rights to the minimum fees.
5. **Optional goodwill asks** if renewal economics reopen: a 60-day vendor renewal reminder and a CPI/3% cap on post-year-one uplifts.
6. **Administrative conform** of the survival cross-reference ("Sections 1 and 5 through 30") once the new insurance section is added.

*We recommend we do not reopen the exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, audit, liquidated damages, governing law, renewal or termination-for-convenience provisions, each of which meets or exceeds our position.*"}

The imbalance is aggravated by the breadth of the Client indemnity in 12(a). *Redline:* expand TrueLink's indemnity to cover third-party IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Client Content, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, plus standard notice, control and cooperation procedure. We left our own indemnity in place as the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position on vendor coverage.

**LOL-CAP (critical).** The only liability limitation, buried at the end of Section 12, caps TrueLink alone at twelve months' hosting and support compensation and is further narrowed to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 only; our liability is uncapped. There is no mutual exclusion of indirect or consequential damages. Our fallback requires a mutual twelve-month fee cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. *Redline:* make the cap mutual and of general application at the greater of twelve months' compensation and USD 1,000,000, add an Excluded Claims carve-out (confidentiality and data security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), and confirm our payment obligations sit outside the limitation.

**ASSIGN (high).** Section 15 is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control language in the document. The clause is mutual and carves out affiliates, but it fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no successor/M&A carve-out, so any merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all our assets requires TrueLink's approval; and approval is absolute rather than subject to a "not unreasonably withheld" standard, so TrueLink could block a corporate transaction outright. *Redline:* add an affiliate/successor carve-out for Client on written notice, apply a reasonableness standard to consent, bar assignment by TrueLink to a Client competitor, and confirm a change of control of Client is neither an assignment nor a termination or re-pricing trigger.

**IP (high).** Section 2(d) confirms TrueLink's rights in the Interface, which is acceptable, but nothing confirms that we retain ownership of Client Content, Client Intellectual Property or our borrower and loan data, and nothing addresses ownership of or a licence to the Section 4 Support Services work product. Section 13's statement that we "shall retain full ownership of all domains associated with Client and Client Content" on discontinuation of Hosting Service is incidental, and Section 10 treats our Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" as Proprietary Information for confidentiality purposes only — which is not an ownership or licence grant. *Redline:* insert a reciprocal Client ownership provision immediately after the existing Ownership clause (assignment of Work Product, licence back for embedded TrueLink IP, no joint ownership). Noted but not separately redlined: Section 8(d)'s licence to exploit "Credit Data" is a term-limited licence over narrowly defined raw third-party data, archived and not combined with Client Proprietary Information and subject to the Non-Competition Agreement — within the negotiated bargain rather than an assignment of our data.

**LICENSE (high).** The Section 2(a) grant runs to "Client" alone; our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are not licensed, and the Exhibit A site-amendment right in Section 2(b)(ii) covers locations only, not additional licensed entities. That fails the fallback of affiliate coverage on written notice. Section 15 also requires consent for any transfer other than to a financially responsible affiliate, so the licence is not transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction as the fallback requires. The licence is not revocable at TrueLink's discretion — Section 2(c) ties it to the term and the Section 13 cut-offs are breach-based — so this is a deviation rather than a walk-away. *Redline:* extend the grant to our affiliates and contractors and add mutual successor-transfer rights.

**WARRANTY (medium).** TrueLink's only express warranty (Section 9) is a Y2K date-processing warranty. There is no conformance-to-documentation warranty, no professional or workmanlike services warranty, no compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranty, and no repair, replace, refund or re-performance remedy. Section 11's "same degree of care, skill and prudence customarily exercised by it for its own operations" is a self-referential standard of care, not a warranty with a remedy, and the disclaimer — while carving out express warranties — leaves nothing meaningful behind. This fails the fallback of 90 days software / 30 days services with remedies. *Redline:* insert an express performance and conformance warranty at the preferred position (12 months software, workmanlike services, no malicious code, compliance with laws) with a repair, replace or refund remedy; the fallback period is negotiable.

**INSURANCE (missing).** A full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the miscellaneous provisions contain no coverage requirement. TrueLink hosts our web site, Client Content and customer credit data. *Redline:* new Section 31 after Force Majeure at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O including tech E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request — with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) flagged in the comment. The survival clause references "Sections 1 and 5 through 30"; a conforming cross-reference update can be handled administratively.

**TRANSITION (missing).** Section 14 fixes only the date services stop. Section 13 puts the burden on us to arrange a new name server within 30 days and new hosting within 60 days, with no TrueLink obligation to assist with migration or to return Client Content, Credit Data or other Client data. Section 10 has no return-or-destroy mechanic and Section 2(f) addresses only TrueLink's own backup practices. Nothing reaches even the fallback of 90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days. *Redline:* insert into Section 14 six months' assistance at then-current rates, return in machine-readable format within 30 days, then deletion with written certification, carved out for legally required retention. The insertion sits in a surviving section under Section 24.

## 3. Walk-away items

The following must be resolved before we can recommend signature:

1. **Uncapped Client liability against a capped Vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12).** Our playbook identifies "Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped" as a walk-away. A mutual cap with the Excluded Claims carve-out, and a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages, is non-negotiable.
2. **No vendor insurance (INSURANCE).** The absence of any coverage requirement for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory under the rule. We require at minimum the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M).
3. **No IP infringement indemnity (INDEMN, § 12).** The vendor indemnity fails even the fallback. Given the absence of any non-infringement warranty, we carry undiluted infringement exposure on a licensed Interface.
4. **Approaching walk-away — assignment consent with no M&A carve-out (ASSIGN, § 15).** An absolute consent right over our merger, acquisition or asset sale approaches the walk-away case of a consent requirement on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out.
